description: North Carolina-only rules checked against Chapter 20 of the General Statutes. National rules stay in the baseline. No fines.

questions.q: A speed limit the North Carolina Department of Transportation sets on an interstate or controlled-access highway
options: Is 75 mph on every rural interstate
Replaces the 35 mph city limit with no signs
questions.explanation: G.S. 20-141(d)(2) lets the Department set a higher maximum on an interstate or controlled-access highway after an engineering and traffic investigation. That limit may not exceed 70 mph. It is not an automatic 70 on every interstate.

questions.q: A lower speed limit on North Carolina school property
options: Is 15 mph statewide with no sign
Is 20 mph whenever a school is nearby
May be set by local ordinance, effective once signs are up
Is the same 35 mph city limit and cannot be lowered
questions.explanation: G.S. 20-141(e1). A public-school limit needs the local school administrative unit's request or consent. A private-school limit needs the school's governing body. The statute does not set one statewide school-zone miles-per-hour number.

questions.q: North Carolina impaired driving includes driving after consuming enough alcohol to have an alcohol concentration of
questions.explanation: G.S. 20-138.1 also covers driving while under the influence of an impairing substance, and driving with any amount of a Schedule I controlled substance or its metabolites.

questions.q: A person under 21 may not drive in North Carolina
options: With any alcohol in the body
Only if a passenger is under 18
questions.explanation: G.S. 20-138.3. A lawfully obtained controlled substance taken in a therapeutically appropriate amount is excepted. The odor of an alcoholic beverage, by itself, is not enough unless the driver was offered a screening test or chemical analysis and refused. While consuming alcohol or while any alcohol previously consumed remains in the body.

questions.q: Impaired driving in a North Carolina commercial motor vehicle includes an alcohol concentration of
questions.explanation: G.S. 20-138.2(a)(2). The offense is not a lesser-included offense of ordinary impaired driving under G.S. 20-138.1.

questions.q: The North Carolina Division may suspend a license when a driver has accumulated
questions.explanation: G.S. 20-16(a)(5). The same subsection also uses eight or more points in the three-year period immediately after reinstatement of a license suspended or revoked for a traffic conviction.

questions.q: On the ordinary North Carolina point schedule, reckless driving is
questions.explanation: G.S. 20-16 assigns 4 points to reckless driving, 5 to passing a stopped school bus, 5 to aggressive driving, and 4 to speeding in a school zone in excess of the posted school-zone limit. The commercial-vehicle schedule in the same section uses different numbers.

questions.q: When a Level 2 holder is not with a supervising driver, passengers under 21 are limited to
options: Any number, if all are under 18
questions.explanation: G.S. 20-11. If a family member or household member under 21 is already a passenger, another under-21 passenger who is not family or household is allowed only when that passenger is a student being driven directly to or from school. No more than one, with the immediate-family and same-household exception.

questions.q: The time, supervision, and passenger limits of Level 1 and Level 2
questions.explanation: G.S. 20-11(g). The mobile-telephone prohibition in G.S. 20-137.3(b) still applies to a full provisional license.

questions.q: In North Carolina, what is the youngest age at which you can get a learner's permit for a car?
questions.explanation: North Carolina issues a learner's permit for a car at 15 years at the earliest.
questions.remember: North Carolina car permit: 15 years at the earliest.

questions.q: In North Carolina, how long must a driver under 18 hold a learner's permit before moving to the next license?
questions.explanation: North Carolina requires drivers under 18 to hold the learner's permit for 9 months.
questions.remember: North Carolina: hold the permit 9 months.

questions.q: How many hours of supervised driving must a teen in North Carolina complete before getting a provisional license?
questions.explanation: North Carolina requires 60 hours of supervised driving before the provisional license.
questions.remember: North Carolina: 60 hours of supervised driving.

provenance.manual: G.S. 20-11. Issuance of limited learner's permit and provisional drivers license to person who is less than 18 years old.

questions.q: Of a North Carolina teen's required supervised driving hours, how many must be at night?
questions.explanation: North Carolina requires at least 10 hours of the supervised driving to be at night.
questions.remember: North Carolina: 10 hours of the supervised driving at night.

provenance.manual: G.S. 20-11. Issuance of limited learner's permit and provisional drivers license to person who is less than 18 years old.

questions.q: In North Carolina, what is the youngest age at which a teen can get a license to drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: In North Carolina, the earliest unsupervised (provisional) license is at 16 years.
questions.remember: North Carolina: driving alone from 16 years.

questions.q: During which hours may a newly licensed teen in North Carolina not drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: North Carolina restricts provisional drivers from 9 p.m. to 5 a.m., with exceptions such as work or school.
questions.remember: North Carolina new drivers: off the road 9 p.m. to 5 a.m..

questions.q: In North Carolina, what is the youngest age for a full, unrestricted car license?
questions.explanation: North Carolina drivers can hold an unrestricted license at 18 years.

provenance.manual: Get a Level 3 Full Provisional License - NCDMV

questions.q: What score do you need to pass the North Carolina car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: You need 80% to pass the North Carolina car knowledge test.
questions.remember: North Carolina car test: pass with 80%.

questions.q: In North Carolina, a driver under 21 breaks the law at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: North Carolina sets the under-21 limit at 0.00%.

provenance.manual: G.S. 20-138.3. Driving by person less than 21 years old after consuming alcohol or drugs.

questions.q: In North Carolina, how long is the license suspension for an adult's first refusal of a breath or blood test?
questions.explanation: A first refusal in North Carolina brings a suspension of 1 year.
questions.remember: North Carolina, first refusal: 1 year without a license.

questions.q: Unless a sign says otherwise, what is the speed limit in a North Carolina residential district?
questions.explanation: North Carolina sets 35 mph in residential districts unless another limit is posted.

questions.q: Which best describes North Carolina's law on drivers using a phone?
options: Phone use is banned only for new or young drivers
No statewide ban on phone use or texting
Hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers
Only texting is banned for all drivers
questions.explanation: North Carolina: only texting is banned for all drivers.
questions.remember: North Carolina phone law: no texting.

provenance.manual: G.S. 20-137.4A. Unlawful use of mobile telephone for text messaging or email.

questions.q: How is North Carolina's seat belt law for adults enforced?
options: Secondary: police can cite you only after stopping you for something else
Primary: police can stop you just for not wearing a seat belt
No seat belt law for adults
questions.explanation: North Carolina seat belt enforcement is primary.
questions.remember: North Carolina seat belts: primary law.

questions.q: Until what age must a child ride in a car seat or booster seat in North Carolina?
questions.explanation: North Carolina requires a car seat or booster until 8 years, with height or weight exceptions.
questions.remember: North Carolina: car or booster seat until 8 years.

questions.q: What is North Carolina's minimum liability insurance (injury per person / injury per crash / property damage)?
questions.explanation: North Carolina requires at least $50,000 / $100,000 / $50,000.

questions.q: Under North Carolina's point system, what is the lowest point total that can suspend an adult's license?
questions.explanation: North Carolina can suspend an adult's license at 12 points in 36 months.
questions.remember: North Carolina suspension: 12 points in 36 months.

provenance.manual: G.S. 20-16. Authority of Division to suspend license.
